questions.question: Which organelle is MOST characteristic of steroid-secreting endocrine cells:
questions.explanation: Smooth ER synthesizes lipids, cholesterol, and steroid molecules.

questions.question: Dotted ribosomes on rough ER chiefly synthesize proteins destined for:

options.A: Secretion, membrane insertion, or specific intracellular compartments

questions.explanation: Rough ER processes proteins targeted for membranes, secretion, or organelles.

questions.question: In the Golgi apparatus, flattened membrane sacs are arranged between a receiving cis face and a shipping:
questions.explanation: Golgi cisternae process cargo from cis face to trans face.

questions.question: Hydrolytic digestion of excess secretory cargo and damaged organelles is executed by:
questions.explanation: Lysosomes supply hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular breakdown.

questions.question: Detoxification of hydrogen peroxide via catalase is a hallmark of:
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes house oxidative enzymes such as catalase.

questions.question: Which organelle holds its OWN DNA in addition to synthesizing ATP:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate ATP on cristae and carry their own DNA.

questions.question: The cylindrical structures inside the centrosome that organize mitotic microtubules are:
questions.explanation: Centrioles associate with centrosomal microtubule organization.

questions.question: Release of stored molecules when a secretory vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane is:
questions.explanation: Secretory vesicles discharge contents outside the cell by exocytosis.

questions.question: Free cytosolic ribosomes primarily translate proteins destined to be secreted by exocytosis.
questions.explanation: ER-bound ribosomes supply secretory and membrane pathways; free ribosomes produce mainly cytosolic proteins.

questions.question: Which cytoskeletal polymers form intracellular transport tracks and cilia:
questions.explanation: Tubulin microtubules build tracks, cilia, and the mitotic spindle.

questions.question: Fibrous cytoskeletal elements supporting mechanical strain and desmosomes are:
questions.explanation: Intermediate filaments resist mechanical tension and connect at desmosomes.

questions.question: Contraction, cell motion, and shape change depend chiefly on:
questions.explanation: Actin-based microfilaments mediate cell shape, motion, contraction, and division.

questions.question: Within the nucleus, ribosomal subunits are produced by one or more:
questions.explanation: Nucleoli assemble ribosomal subunits from rRNA and proteins.

questions.question: During mitosis, dispersed nuclear chromatin condenses visibly into:
questions.explanation: Chromatin fibers compact into chromosomes during division.

questions.question: A cell dying after severe toxic exposure typically undergoes:
questions.explanation: Toxic injury, trauma, infection, or ischemia cause necrosis.

questions.question: Which physiological process relies on APOPTOSIS:

options.A: Removal of tissue between developing digits
options.B: Elimination of excess neurons during maturation

questions.explanation: Apoptosis sculpts digits and refines neuronal and immune populations.

questions.question: Which comparison between free and ER-bound ribosomes is TRUE:

options.A: Free ribosomes make cytosolic proteins; ER-bound feed secretion
options.B: Free ribosomes operate without mRNA templates

questions.explanation: Ribosome location determines whether proteins stay in cytosol or enter ER secretory/membrane pathways.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of the endomembrane protein shipping pathway:
questions.explanation: Secretory proteins route through rough ER, Golgi, and secretory vesicles, not cristae.

questions.question: In cell biology, 'ectoplasm' refers specifically to:
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm can be divided descriptively into outer ectoplasm and deeper endoplasm.

questions.question: The nucleolus assembles ribosomal subunits inside the nucleus before export to the cytoplasm.
questions.explanation: One or more nucleoli produce ribosomal subunits from rRNA and proteins.

questions.question: Cholesterol in the plasma membrane helps regulate membrane stability and flexibility.
questions.explanation: Cholesterol stabilizes phospholipid packing and modulates flexibility.

questions.question: Skeletal muscle fibers are completely devoid of nuclei just like mature red blood cells.
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle fibers contain multiple nuclei, whereas mature RBCs are anucleate.

questions.question: Peroxisomes primarily digest engulfed bacteria through hydrolytic enzymes.
questions.explanation: Lysosomes digest phagocytosed material via hydrolytic enzymes; peroxisomes oxidize peroxide and fatty acids.

questions.question: Pathological necrosis typically follows severe injury and promotes surrounding inflammation.
questions.explanation: Necrotic disruption releases cellular contents that provoke inflammation in adjacent tissues.
